sources.label: Axiom V2 — ZK-verified historical queries (fixed on-chain verify)
Groth16 on-chain verification gas (BN254 pairing precompiles)
Brevis Pico Prism 2.0 — real-time Ethereum proving

presets.label: 30-day TWAP
presets.note: Time-weighted price from 720 hourly observations. The values are historical — older than the 8191-block (~27h) window the EVM can still see — so a contract can't recompute them on-chain at all.

presets.label: 90-day holding proof
presets.note: Did this address hold ≥ N tokens across 90 daily snapshots? Loyalty / sybil-resistant airdrops. Ninety historical balances, none reachable from current state.

presets.label: Foreign-chain slot
presets.note: Prove one Base storage slot to a contract on Ethereum. Only one value — but the EVM cannot read another chain's state at any price. Re-execution isn't expensive here, it's impossible.

presets.label: A year of transfers
presets.note: Aggregate an address's activity across a year of blocks (~2.63M at 12s/block). Even if the state were reachable, the read alone is ~6.0B gas — a hundred Ethereum blocks of nothing but SLOADs.

presets.label: 120 live balances
presets.note: A snapshot of 120 balances in the current block. This the EVM *can* do — 120 cold reads ≈ 297k gas with the base tx — which is exactly the break-even against a coprocessor proof. Below this, read on-chain; above it (or back in time), prove.
